panels.title: Consensus height (slot / committed / applied)
panels.description: A growing gap between slot and last_applied means blocks are committing faster than the fact engine applies them.

panels.title: Incoming transaction rate (submitted)
panels.description: Append attempts per second on each node (the submit rate). Reuses the cumulative quod_consensus_submitted counter.

panels.title: Commit & apply rate
panels.description: Blocks committed vs facts applied per second. commits is per committing node; applies is universal (member + follower via the feed).

panels.title: Transaction processing time (submit → commit)
panels.description: Percentiles of block.timestamp − tx.submitted_at, from the quod_tx_commit_latency_ms histogram. Observed on the committing node (accurate at N=1 where submitter == committer).

panels.title: Committed transactions by author
panels.description: Per-submitting-node committed-tx rate (author = the node that originated the write). Driven by the live {committed,Ns} event.

panels.title: Write size (asserts + retracts per tx)
panels.description: Percentiles of the diff size per committed transaction (quod_tx_diff_ops histogram).

panels.title: In-flight writes (pending appends / parked)
panels.description: Liveness: consensus appends awaiting commit, and quod_prolog writes parked awaiting their verdict. Sustained non-zero = writes not committing.

panels.title: Active proofs & selected scopes
panels.description: Origin proofs and reusable selected-ontology scopes running on this node. Each scope retains one frozen base plus its proof-local changes until the origin proof closes it.

panels.title: Knowledge-base memory & retained history
panels.description: Shared knowledge-base ETS memory (left axis, Erlang VM words) and predicates retaining an older version (right axis). Retained history should fall back to 0 after frozen queries finish; persistent growth points to slow or stuck queries.

panels.title: Append rejections by reason
panels.description: Failure outcomes: redirect means the local consensus process was unavailable, the receiver did not own the declared target slot, or that slot had already closed; it should stay near zero. bad means malformed or unauthorized content. busy is an ALERT signal: the bounded ingress line overflowed or a waiting request expired during a genuine stall. stale_seq means newer approved history superseded an otherwise-valid signed request. retry shows the caller-visible requests that must run Prolog and submit again, split by cause.

panels.title: Ingress queue and relay retries
panels.description: Requests waiting for consensus and relay retry health. accepted/s means a destination acknowledged receipt and fast retries stopped. redrives/s recovers dropped requests or result hints; duplicates/s is work that reached the consensus mailbox unnecessarily and should stay low. forwarded/s counts locally queued requests dispatched when their exact target slot became available. Overflow and expiry are genuine overload or stall signals.

panels.title: Write conflicts, rejects and unresolved deadlines
panels.description: OCC conflicts and apply-time rejects are definite failures. An unresolved deadline means the local caller stopped waiting before the transaction's final result was known; it may still commit and must not be retried blindly.

panels.title: Feed: blocks sent out (per node)
panels.description: How many final blocks each node produced and started sending to the rest of the network, per second.

panels.title: Feed: blocks received & relayed (per node)
panels.description: How many blocks each node received from others, checked, applied and passed along, per second.

panels.title: Feed: catch-up pulls (per node)
panels.description: How often each node had to ask others for blocks it was missing, per second.

panels.title: Feed drops — actionable
panels.description: Unexpected feed drops. gap = out-of-order and re-pulled by anti-entropy; unverified = bad certificate; ingest_busy and oversized also require investigation. This panel should normally stay at zero.

panels.title: Feed ignores — expected
panels.description: Expected feed traffic ignored by consensus participants or gossip deduplication. non_following is normal when validators receive feed copies of blocks that consensus already applies; duplicate is benign redundant gossip.

panels.title: Peers known (per node)
panels.description: How many other nodes each node currently knows about.

panels.title: Gossip sample size (per node)
panels.description: How many known nodes each node is actively sharing updates with, so gossip stays even.

panels.title: Open connections (per node)
panels.description: How many other nodes each node has an open connection to right now.

panels.title: Committee size (nodes allowed to vote)
panels.description: How many nodes are currently allowed to vote on changes. Every node should report the same value.

panels.title: Voter or observer, per node (1 = can vote)
panels.description: 1 if the node is allowed to vote, 0 if it only reads and follows along.

panels.title: Admission readiness (liveness digests)
panels.description: On a committee member: how many peers it tracks a liveness heartbeat for (digests) and how many are FRESH right now (fresh_digests). A candidate must be fresh here before it can be admitted. Confirm this is non-zero for the candidate before an admit.

panels.title: Finality watchdog state
panels.description: State of the oldest unfinished block on each node. phase: 0 idle, 1 waiting for a proposal, 2 waiting for support, 3 waiting for final commit votes. quorum_ready is 1 when enough linked validators have freshly reported that they are caught up to this node; complaint voting pauses while it is 0.

panels.title: Consensus recovery activity
panels.description: Recovery work per second: proposal/finality redrives, oldest-head watchdog expirations, complaints paused during a known below-quorum outage, weak-certificate waits, and invalid membership proposals. These should stay near zero in steady state; a burst should return to zero after connectivity recovers.

panels.title: Finality vote camps
panels.description: Votes each node currently knows for the oldest unfinished block. Support votes approve a block, commit votes make it final, and skip votes abandon the slot. Commit and skip both stuck below the committee quorum reveal a split finality round. own skip is 1 on validators locked to the skip side; missing block means the node has an approval certificate but is still retrieving the block's transactions.

panels.title: Vote journal disk sync time
panels.description: Median and 95th-percentile time to make one validator vote crash-durable before sending its signature. A healthy block normally needs one support sync and one final-vote sync per validator; sustained high values directly add to block finality time.

panels.title: Author signature check time
panels.description: Median and 95th-percentile time each node spends checking one transaction author's Ed25519 signature before voting. A sustained rise means authentication is consuming more of the block-processing budget.

panels.title: Invalid author signatures rejected
panels.description: Rate of transactions rejected because the author's cryptographic signature did not match the signed content. This should stay at zero; any increase means corrupted, malformed, or dishonest input reached a validator.

panels.title: Node logs — warnings & errors (Loki)
panels.description: Live warning/error/notice log lines from every quod node. Each node emits one JSON object per event to stdout (quod_log_formatter); promtail ships it as {job="docker"} and Loki's | json exposes level/msg/node_id. node_id (kp_…) names the emitting instance — same id as the $node picker.

panels.title: Runtime (P tier)
panels.description: Derived working state per node. healthy is 1 while handlers are live; e_frontier should track the committed height (effects for a block are released only once the frontier reaches it); collapses climbing means ordered handler work keeps being rebuilt; heavy failures are isolated resource rebuild failures; heavy rejected means a job exceeded the size limit or the bounded pending-resource queue was full; rejected dynamic means someone tried to install running code after founding.

panels.title: Consensus performance — how fast the nodes agree on a block
Block agreement time - the two halves (this node's blocks)
panels.description: When it is this node's turn to build a block, the two stages of getting it agreed: 'accept' is until enough other nodes approve it, 'make final' is until it is saved for good. Add the two lines for the total time one block takes. On a fast local network each should be tens of milliseconds.

panels.title: Where a block's time is spent, by step (slowest first)
panels.description: Each block is handled in a series of small steps (saving a vote to disk, saving the block, sending it on, and so on). This shows how long each step takes at the 99th percentile. When a block is slow, the step with the tallest line is the reason - for example 'support' and 'persist' were the disk-write steps that the storage fix made ~40x faster.

panels.title: Time to handle one message
panels.description: How long this node takes to deal with a single incoming message (a proposal, a vote, and so on), by kind. These should stay small (a few milliseconds). If they stay small but blocks are still slow, the delay is elsewhere - the network or waiting on other nodes.

panels.title: Messages waiting in line (backlog)
panels.description: How many messages are already queued up waiting when this node picks up the next one. This should be near zero. A number that climbs means messages are arriving faster than the node can handle them, so work backs up - this is the signal that showed a burst of transactions briefly overwhelming a node.

panels.title: Time to collect votes from the other nodes
panels.description: When this node builds a block, how long from sending it out until each other node's vote comes back. This is the plain round-trip time to gather agreement; it sets the floor for how fast a block can be made final.

panels.title: Discarded messages (should stay flat at zero)
panels.description: Messages this node threw away instead of sending, per second, by bounded channel class and reason. log is consensus, ingress is retained relay traffic, and other covers all non-Simplex links. 'flow_control' means the receiving node was too slow to accept more; 'queue_full' means this node's own send buffer was full. A discarded message is re-sent later by a timer, so any sustained rate here quietly slows agreement down. Flat at zero is healthy.

panels.title: Network connections (one line per other node)
Round-trip time per connection (typical vs best-ever)
panels.description: For each connection to another node: 'typical' is the current estimate of how long a message-and-reply takes, 'best' is the fastest ever seen (the raw network speed). On a local network both should be a few milliseconds. A big gap - typical much higher than best - means something is adding delay on top of the network (a busy machine or slow replies).

panels.title: Data buffered inside connections (hidden delay)
panels.description: Bytes sitting inside the network connections instead of being delivered: 'waiting to send' has not left this node yet, 'sent, unconfirmed' is on the wire but not acknowledged. Both near zero is healthy. If 'waiting to send' stays above zero, the connection is holding messages back and adding delay the application cannot see.

panels.title: Transactions per proposed block
panels.description: How effectively proposers pack transactions together. Average is the exact fleet ratio; p50 and p95 show the distribution of individual proposed blocks. Under sustained load, values near 1 mean transactions are missing the same collection window and creating avoidable blocks.

panels.title: Batch collection wait
panels.description: How long each proposer actually kept a block open to collect transactions. Ordinary blocks should approach the configured window; full and membership blocks seal early. This is intentional batching delay, not consensus or disk latency.
